_comment: Fares were read off the National Rail journey planner for named dates, so they
are 'what the planner quoted', which is what a reader will see. Bus times come
from the operator's own live timetable feed (Pulhams is operated by Go-Ahead and
publishes through oxfordbus.co.uk) or from the operator's own PDF. Parking comes
from the district or county council that owns the car park. Attraction prices
come from the attraction's own site or its own booking API - no aggregators.

gettingThere._note: All returns quoted for Tue 15 Sep 2026, out mid-morning, back 18:00-19:00. Singles quoted for Tue 13 Oct 2026 (a month out) to test for Advance fares.

stations.offPeakReturnNote: Quoted from the 10:53 departure onwards. The 09:52 and departures from 15:23 were quoted at £72.00, and the 16:58 at £106.00.
stations.singleNote: Every departure on Tue 13 Oct 2026 was quoted at the same £53.00, so the planner offered no Advance bargain. GWR's own booking engine quoted an Anytime Day Single of £53.60 for travel on 12 Sep 2026 and no Off-Peak or Advance fare at all that day. The practical reading: the return costs about £1 more than a single, so always buy the return.
stations.lastTrainBackWeekday: 23:31, arriving Paddington 01:16. Last sensible one 21:46, in at 23:29.
stations.putsYouWithin: Moreton town centre is a two-minute walk from the platform. Batsford Arboretum is 1.9 miles / 44 minutes on foot via Arboretum Walk (Google Maps, walking). Everything else needs the 801 bus, which calls at the station.

stations.note: Cheaper and faster than Moreton-in-Marsh, and the Cotswold Motoring Museum's own travel page puts Kingham 5 miles from Bourton against Moreton's 8. But no useful bus connects it, so it is a taxi station.

stations.putsYouWithin: Cirencester, 12 minutes on Stagecoach 882 (Kemble Railway Station 11:50 -> Cirencester Old Station Car Park 12:02). Only about five or six journeys a day, Monday to Saturday, and the published timetable has no Sunday column.
Stroud itself - a working Five Valleys market town, not a chocolate-box village. No village of the postcard kind is within walking distance.

stations.offPeakReturnNote: Cheapest of the five. Departures from 15:23 were quoted at £60.70 and from 16:58 at £92.20.
stations.putsYouWithin: Charlbury itself: Market Street is 0.3 mile / 9 minutes from the station on foot (Google Maps, walking). Nothing else is walkable.

stations.offPeakReturn: £70.90 direct, £78.10 on the routes with a change
stations.putsYouWithin: Cheltenham. The reason to come here is Royal Well bus station, where the 801, 606 and X52 all start - 1.1 miles / 25 minutes on foot from the railway station (Google Maps, walking).

bibury.parishCouncil: Bibury Parish Council: 'public parking is limited in Bibury, there is some parking bays provided by Gloucestershire County Council - opposite the Trout Farm (including Two Coach Bays) and along The Street.' (page last updated 2019)
bibury.nationalTrust: National Trust Bibury page: 'Free parking opposite the Trout Farm and along the Highway (not National Trust). Can be busy.' Sat nav GL7 5NP.
bibury.arlingtonRowAccess: National Trust, in its own words: 'Please take care to respect the privacy of residents living in Arlington Row and be aware that vehicular access is restricted to residents because of the steep and narrow access road and the lack of turning or parking space.' The cottages are private homes; Nos. 1 and 9 are National Trust holiday lets; there is no public access to the cottages or gardens.
bibury.coachBaysRemoved: Gloucestershire County Council, reviewed 25 July 2025: the coach parking bays in the centre of Bibury have been removed and replaced with a bus stop clearway with a 10-minute wait limit. Coaches are asked to turn round at Cirencester services, which GCC concedes 'adds 15-20 minutes to journey times'.
bibury.paidAlternative: Bibury Trout Farm charges £10 for its car park.

castleCombe.detail: Pay-and-display car park in Dunns Lane, Upper Castle Combe. 'Enforcement officers regularly patrol to monitor and deter illegal parking in the village.' Visitors are asked not to park across businesses or private residences or on yellow lines.

broadwayTower.charges: £3 for up to 4 hours, £6 all day, pay and display

bourtonOnTheWater.what: The River Windrush runs through the middle under low stone footbridges. Three paid attractions on one street plus the green.
bourtonOnTheWater.crowding: Bourton-on-the-Water Parish Council, 9 September 2025: 'the increased visitor numbers this year have placed significant pressure not only on the village centre but also on surrounding residential and commercial areas' and 'The Parish Council has no control over visitor numbers and has no power to close the village.' An Experimental Traffic Regulation Order on Meadow Way to manage coach traffic was due to run for a year to September 2026. The council also says Gloucestershire Highways has refused a residents' parking permit scheme.

stowOnTheWold.what: Market square at the top of the hill where the Fosse Way crosses, antique shops, St Edward's Church with its yew-flanked north door. The 801 stops at the Library.

lowerSlaughter.what: The Old Mill on the River Eye, a lane of stone cottages and no through traffic.
lowerSlaughter.walk: Bourton-on-the-Water to Lower Slaughter to Upper Slaughter is 2.6 miles and about 58 minutes on foot, mostly flat (Google Maps, walking).

bibury.what: Arlington Row (National Trust, c.1380 as a monastic wool store, converted to weavers' cottages in the 17th century), the Rack Isle water meadow, and Bibury Trout Farm.

broadway.what: A wide green High Street; Broadway Tower on the escarpment a mile above the village; Snowshill Manor is signed from here.

chippingCampden.what: The Market Hall on the High Street, built 1627 by Sir Baptist Hicks, Grade I listed and given to the National Trust in the 1940s; free to walk through. The northern end of the Cotswold Way.
chippingCampden.cotswoldWay: 102 miles / 164 km, Chipping Campden to Bath (National Trails).

burford.what: One long High Street dropping to a bridge over the Windrush; free council parking; on the X52 between Oxford and Cheltenham.

cirencester.what: A Roman town - Corinium - with the Corinium Museum, St John Baptist parish church and the Abbey Grounds. The hub of the 855 and the 882.

castleCombe.what: In Wiltshire, on the southern edge of the Cotswolds, 12 miles from Bath. Nothing in the north Cotswolds pairs with it in a day.

getYourGuide.inventoryNote: The inventory records 47 Cotswolds products and notes that nothing in the Cotswolds needs an entry ticket, so the conditional-inclusion problem that dogs other destinations does not apply - which is why it calls the Cotswolds the cleanest destination to sell. It also records that the Cotswolds is one of only three destinations in the inventory that is realistically not doable by train instead.

notFound: Blenheim Palace admission prices - the site's ticket pages render prices only inside a JavaScript booking engine and no public JSON endpoint was reachable, so Blenheim is left out of the article.
Snowshill Manor's closed days of the week - the National Trust opening calendar is drawn by JavaScript and the underlying data was not reachable from the page source.
